Hi Priya,

Thanks for onboarding Redwood as our custody/settlement partner. Attached is our June invoice for platform and transaction fees. Our AP team has a couple of questions on the VAT side before we submit payment:

1) CoinBridge is an EU-registered exchange (VAT ID on page 2 of the attached PDF). We are uncertain whether the transaction and platform fees should be charged with VAT, or if the reverse-charge applies when the recipient (Redwood) is outside the EU.
2) Does Redwood accept invoices with a self-billing or marketplace-style allocation (CoinBridge issues a single invoice that splits fees across multiple service lines and beneficiaries)? If so, do you need us to sign a self-billing agreement?
3) Our local tax advisors (LedgerPartners VAT in cc) recommended we confirm the correct place-of-supply rule for crypto trading fees and whether VAT is due on settlement services.

Could you confirm Redwood's billing treatment and whether you require any additional documentation to validate VAT ID and allow payment release? We are keen to avoid payment delays.

Attachments: CoinBridge_Invoice_2026-06.pdf (application/pdf), CoinBridge_VAT_Registration.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks,

Hi Marta — thanks for sending and for including LedgerPartners.

Short answer: Redwood typically treats platform and settlement fees billed to corporate customers as B2B services. If CoinBridge is VAT-registered in an EU member state and the invoice is to Redwood (US entity) for B2B services, the reverse-charge mechanism often applies (no VAT charged by you; Redwood accounts for VAT locally where required). That said, crypto-specific guidance can vary by country and by how the service is characterized.

What we need from you to proceed without a payment hold:
- A copy of the VAT registration extract (we have CoinBridge_VAT_Registration.pdf already — thanks).
- Confirmation of the billing legal entity and the billing address used on the invoice.
- If you want Redwood to accept a self-billing arrangement, please send your proposed self-billing agreement; our legal/finance will review. To speed things up, LedgerPartners can send a short memo confirming the recommended place-of-supply classification.

Soojin (cc) — can you please: 1) validate the VAT ID against VIES and LedgerPartners' memo, 2) put a temporary payment note on the invoice until we confirm, and 3) flag whether we need a vendor self-billing signature?

Karthik — FYI: this is CoinBridge (prospect turning customer) — they asked about allocation across beneficiaries (marketplace/self-billing). They prefer a single invoice split across service lines. If we accept that, we just need a signed self-billing acknowledgment.

Marta — once Soojin confirms the VAT ID we'll update you and aim to release payment within 3 business days.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
priya.n@redwood.com
